pre_execution_findings.finding: The isolated generation package required structured facts but did not provide the target evaluator's executable public fact vocabulary or a frozen semantic adapter contract.
pre_execution_findings.consequence: The generated domain-record facts cannot be assumed to be valid executable inputs to the frozen target evaluator.

pre_execution_findings.finding: The package did not provide the frozen target evaluator's public violation-code vocabulary, so the generator created its own G3 requirement-level semantic codes.
pre_execution_findings.consequence: The preregistered ALL_REQUIRED_CODES_PRESENT rule cannot be applied directly without an unregistered translation layer.

pre_execution_findings.finding: 19 of 27 MUST_REJECT cases require more than one semantic violation code, while the generation package does not define how primary and secondary requirement violations are to be executed and combined.
pre_execution_findings.consequence: Creating that scoring interpretation after target execution would permit post-outcome rule construction.

interpretation: Generation Attempt 1 is preserved exactly but rejected before any target-evaluator execution because the isolated generation package did not define a complete executable interface and violation-scoring contract. This disposition is based on test-interface admissibility, not on any target prediction or holdout outcome. No case, evaluator, prediction, or scientific result is rewritten.
